raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I've been working this land in Quzhou for over 30 years. My father grew wheat and maize on these same fields, and I'll do the same. The North China Plain loam here is made for winter wheat followed by summer maize — that double-cropping rotation is what I know, what the grain buyers expect, and what the weather and soils here support. I'm not going to gamble on cash crops I don't know. Cotton prices have been bad and the labor is brutal. I'll stick with what feeds my family and pays the bills.

I have about 10 mu. Nine goes to the wheat-maize rotation. I'll keep 1 mu for garlic — I can sell it at the Quzhou market in late spring and it fits between wheat cycles on a small patch near the house.

For wheat seed I'll use Jimai 22 — the township extension office promoted it and my neighbor has done well with it. Good lodging resistance, decent yield. For maize I always use Zhengdan 958 hybrid, same as most people around here. It's reliable.

Fertilizer: I'll put down compound base fertilizer before wheat planting, then urea top-dressing at jointing. Maize gets basal fertilizer at planting and a side-dressing at the big bell stage. These are the rates I've been using for years — they work.

Water worries me most. Every year the well goes deeper. But wheat in this dry spring climate needs at least three waterings — winter freeze water, jointing, and grain filling. Maize usually gets enough from summer rain, but I'll run the pump once at tasseling if it's dry.

Pesticides: wheat gets herbicide in winter and a fungicide-insecticide spray in late spring for powdery mildew and aphids. Maize gets a post-emergence herbicide and one spray for corn borer if I see damage.
